reason: Re-opened packet.js pali 4: Story IV.5 (Niggardly Kosiya, Norman [373] to [376]) has the Teacher in the Hall of Truth say verbatim that a monk who would convert a household without impairing faith or riches must approach it to make known the virtues of the Buddha as a bee approaches a flower, then speak verse 49; the paraphrase (wins a household over, makes the Buddha’s virtues known, without impairing its faith or riches) is carried whole. The Pali Tattha on 49 agrees (Na hi tassa gāme caraṇapaccayā kulānaṃ saddhāhāni vā bhogahāni vā honti). Plain sense true to day.js (47 and 48 are death seizing the distracted flower-gatherer; 49 turns to the sage) and repeats no four words of the verse. IV.5 is the right story; Buddhist Legends part 2 is HOS 29, Books III to XII. verse.js ok (Dhammapada 49, at 48); entry-check ok. Note only: the Pali adds Idha pana khīṇāsavova adhippeto (the arahant is meant here), not needed for the story’s lesson.
